open_points.subject: Model M09 — AuditEntry identity
open_points.text: “the sequence number is what tells them apart” versus “A store restored from a backup after a loss begins its own history from the backup's last number”
open_points.question: When the original and restored histories mint different AuditEntries with the same sequence number, what is an AuditEntry's identity across histories, and does a store history itself have an identity recorded by Registry?
options: The sequence identifies an entry only within the current store history; abandoned histories are outside the model
AuditEntry identity is the pair of a recorded store-history identity and sequence number
Sequence numbers remain unique across histories through a high-water mark kept outside the restored backup
open_points.default_guess: Treat the sequence as identity only within the current store history and add no persisted history identity.

open_points.subject: Model M10 — MigrationClosure ownership and cardinality
open_points.text: “it is a fact about the instance” and “Durable, at most one per instance” versus “present for the rest of the store's history” and “the import may then be made again” after restoration
open_points.question: Does MigrationClosure belong to the Registry instance or to one store history, and can the same continuing instance create a second closure after restoring a pre-import backup?
options: It belongs to a store history; one instance may create closures in successive histories, with at most one in each
A restored store is a new Registry instance, preserving at most one closure per instance
It belongs permanently to the deployment and must survive or be reconstructed even when the restored backup predates it
open_points.default_guess: Treat MigrationClosure as belonging to a store history, with at most one closure in the currently restored history.
